text.p: Leading stories in the Greek press:
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--Final poll results show Simitis rid of 'proedriki' supporters aligned to PASOK founder, the late Andreas Papandreou.
--Poll analysis: Voters in rural areas bolster two-party system while urban voters more willing to share their vote amongst other parties.
--Parliament to see 111 new faces.

--Five tendencies battle it out for the leadership of the main opposition party New Democracy following Sunday's election defeat and resignation by leader Miltiades Evert. Evert's intentions remain "an enigma".
--Existential questions at Political Spring party following its poor electoral performance and failure to get into Parliament.
ETHNOS

--The positioning of five key ministers will determine the face of the new Simitis government. Gerasimos Arsenis to be moved - unwillingly - from national defence, in favour of Akis Tsohatzopoulos or George Papandreou. Evangelos Yiannopoulos to go from labour to justice while Simitis tries to convince Papadopoulos to stay put at the finance ministry, despite his wanting to work on public administration at the interior ministry.
--Seventy seats change hands in Sunday's elections with many high-profile names losing out.
TA NEA
--Crucial talks for Simitis today as changes in key ministries appear to be on the cards. Decision on new cabinet ready by tomorrow at the latest.

--New Democracy deputy Kostas Karamanlis's possible run for leadership of the party, with the support of Evert, has delayed announcements of candidacy by party deputy president Ioannis Varvitsiotis and former education minister George Souflias.
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS
--Evert insists on his resignation. Varvitsiotis, Souflias and Karamanlis decide today, following announcements by Dora Bakoyianni and Stephanos Manos.
KATHIMERINI

--Markets greet socialist election victory with reservations. Increased leftist presence in new Parliament tied to fears that government will be restricted from going ahead with an aggressive economic policy.

--Former finance minister Alekos Papadopoulos insists on moving from ministry: reports say Yannos Papandoniou may take over both finance and economy portfolios, or former development minister Vasso Papandreou to move to economy ministry.
--Main opposition New Democracy on the boil, following Sunday's defeat and leader Miltiades Evert's resignation. More challengers expected to declare that they will join the race for president today.
--The face of Parliament changes, as 108 former MPs miss out on re-election.
--Time of the essence, say international analysts. Prime Minister Costas Simitis is called on to meet the difficult invitation to quickly realise his promises of a stronger, more competitive economy.
--Business world says there will be no honeymoon period for new government. Simitis has no excuse to delay economic convergence and expansion, following Sunday's mandate.
--Concern at telecoms organisation (OTE) for its investment programme if Greece is taken to European Court for infringement of rules of competition.
--Finance ministry's first move is to push through draft legislation changing customs code.
--National Bank's programme to sell stake in own subsidiaries to others, increase share capital and write off old debts to be applied.
IMERISIA

--Simitis expected to announce new cabinet today. Sources say Yannos Papandoniou and Vasso Papandreou the big guns in the new government's economic ministries, supported by new faces in undersecretary positions.

--Senior economic experts committee to be established to examine the economy's problems and suggest solutions for the economy's adjustment to economic and monetary union (EMU). Other items on the agenda for the committee: management of state assets and modernisation of stock exchange to better facilitate increased privatisations.
--Money market reacts favourably: interbank rates fall, T-bills stable.
--Business wants all election pledges met. Industry and commerce stress that emphasis must be laid on course to convergence, cutbacks on spending and the state, and no new taxes.
KERDOS
--New Democracy searches for a "leader of unity": Dora Bakoyianni and former conservative economy minister Stephanos Manos first to throw glove in the ring.

--Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) calls for a "tough budget" with emphasis on restricted public spending and increased privatisation, as a first indication the new government is serious about putting country on track for both nominal and real convergence.
--High liquidity in the interbank market.
--Economy ministers push through new bill restricting state spending, aimed at saving the state 250 billion drachmas.
EXPRESS

--Favourable conditions for the success of the new government. Papandoniou expected to remain at national economy ministry, while Papadopulos insists on moving from finance ministry, though this is not certain.
--Money market sees forex inflows, increase in drachma parity, fall in interest rates.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Business demands the new government stick to the convergence programme. Developments on political scene - and composition of new government - will be indicative of prevailing atmosphere.
--Commission President Jacques Santer welcomes PASOK's election win and calls for "bold decisions" to be taken for the modernisation of the Greek economy.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom, +301 331812-4
